content.comment_body: Hello, I'm having trouble controlling [product_name] PLC via SMS. I can control outputs Q1 and Q2 on the [product_name] by sending commands like [product_name];OUTPUT,O1,1 and [product_name];OUTPUT=O1,1. However, when I attempt to control PLC flags or similar functions using network input, the response SMS says "No Success". I've also tried using SMS alias without a password. Please refer to the attached file.

To use the BYTE datatype, the correct syntax is: Password;[product_name]=VM6,1,Byte (sets bit V6.0 high) and Password;[product_name]=VM6,0,Byte (sets bit V6.0 low). With BYTE, only the first bit of the Byte can be addressed. For BIT datatype, the syntax is: Password;[product_name]=VM6.0,1,Bit (sets bit V6.0 high) and Password;[product_name]=VM6.0,0,Bit (sets bit V6.0 low). Here, each bit in the Byte can be controlled individually. Another example: Password;[product_name]=VM2.3,1,Bit sets V2.3 high, Password;[product_name]=VM2.3,0,Bit sets V2.3 low. These datatypes only work with the appropriate firmware for the [product_name]. If your [product_name]'s version is not [version_no], update its firmware. Firmware updates for [product_name] are available at [url]. To use BIT datatype, ensure your [product_name] is FS04 or newer and the firmware is FW V1.81.01 or higher.
Hi, thanks for the quick reply. I need to update the firmware versions. Please see the current firmware versions for [product_name] and [product_name] in the attached file.

The [product_name] firmware is FS05 (V1.81.02), which is acceptable. However, there is a newer update available for FS06. Check the product information for firmware updates for [product_name] 8 FS:04 and FS:05 at [url].
The setup is now functioning correctly.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered difficulty controlling PLC internal flags via SMS with [product_name]. SMS commands successfully operated outputs, but setting internal flags returned an error message. This was caused by incorrect SMS syntax and outdated firmware versions on both the [product_name] and [product_name] modules. Updating firmware solved the control issue.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect reliable control of outputs and internal PLC flags via SMS, utilizing standard documented command syntax and supported features.
